overall: The AG found the Swansea Board of Assessors violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to respond to an executive session minutes request within 10 days and by missing complaint-response deadlines; accessibility and abatement-notice claims were rejected.

allegations.summary: Board did not respond within 10 days to a request for executive session minutes from 2020-2024 (request limited on review to executive sessions).
allegations.key_passage: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law when it failed to respond to the complainant’s request for executive session minutes within 10 days of his request.

allegations.summary: Board did not respond within 14 business days to Open Meeting Law complaints filed February 19 and March 7.
allegations.key_passage: The Board’s responded to the complaints of February 19 and March 7 on April 22, much later than the 14-day deadline imposed by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: March 13 meeting held in Town Hall room allegedly too small (five chairs) and not wheelchair accessible.
allegations.key_passage: The complainant has not detailed a specific incident when he or another member of the public was denied access to a Board meeting.

allegations.summary: Meeting notice for March 13 executive session allegedly improperly listed names and addresses of abatement applicants.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Open Meeting Law does not itself require that abatement applications remain confidential, we find that the Board did not violate the Law when it identified the owner and address of properties being considered for abatements.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the law's requirements
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
